body.statement: For every revealed \(d_n\)-regular graph with \(M_n<n\), the seed design and observed-data Rao--Blackwell estimator are unbiased for \(\tau_n\), and \[Q_G=\sum_{r=1}^{k_n}\binom{k_n}{r}K_G^{\circ r}\succeq0,\qquad \sup_{y\in\mathcal M_n(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}-\tau_n)^2\mid G]\le U(G,k_n).\] Every entry of \(Q_G\), every weight \(w_i(z;G)\), and the certificate are finite graph computations from \(G\) and \(k_n\).
body.justification: The exact Schur-power identity is the two-arm covariance mechanism that prevents the control estimator from paying the generic conflict spectral radius.
body.gap: KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, Theorem 4.1, uses randomized priority resolution and a generic conflict-graph norm; UganderYin2023RGCR, Theorem 4.8, studies bounded outcomes within randomized cluster designs. Neither gives this endpoint-\(L_2\) certificate.
body.consumer: A revealed network can be randomized once and audited before outcomes arrive by evaluating the displayed graph-only certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\) with \(M_n<n\), and abbreviate \(B=B_2(G)\), \(P=P_n\), \(m_i=m_i(G)\), \(q_i=q_i(G)\), \(\pi_i=\pi_i(G)\), and \(k=k_n\).  The radius-two row support of \(B\) is \(S_i=\{v:\operatorname{dist}_G(i,v)\le2\}\), with \(|S_i|=m_i\).  Since a \(d_n\)-regular graph has at most \(1+d_n+d_n(d_n-1)=d_n^2+1=M_n\) vertices within distance two of a vertex,
\[
q_i=1-m_i/n\ge1-M_n/n>0,
\qquad
\pi_i=q_i^k>0.
\tag{10}
\]

Introduce the augmented estimators
\[
U_1=\frac1k\sum_{\ell=1}^ka_{J_\ell},
\qquad
U_0=\frac1n\sum_{i\in V_n}\frac{\mathbf 1\{i\in C_G(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})\}b_i}{\pi_i}.
\]
Every seed \(J_\ell\) is fully treated because \(N_G[J_\ell]\) is included in the treated union.  A unit \(i\) is fully control-exposed exactly when every seed avoids \(S_i\).  Uniform independent seed draws and (10) therefore give
\[
\mathbb E(U_1\mid G)=\mu_1,
\quad
\operatorname{Var}(U_1\mid G)=\frac1k\operatorname{Var}(a_{J_1}\mid G)
\le\frac1{kn}\sum_i a_i^2\le\frac1k,
\tag{11}
\]
and \(\mathbb E(U_0\mid G)=\mu_0\).

Put \(h_{ij}=|S_i\cap S_j|=(BB^{\mathsf T})_{ij}\).  Independence of the \(k\) seeds gives
\[
\frac{\Pr(i,j\in C_G(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})\mid G)}{\pi_i\pi_j}
=\left\{\frac{1-(m_i+m_j-h_{ij})/n}{q_iq_j}\right\}^{k}
=\left\{1+\frac{h_{ij}-m_im_j/n}{nq_iq_j}\right\}^{k}.
\tag{12}
\]
Since \((BPB^{\mathsf T})_{ij}=h_{ij}-m_im_j/n\), the last fraction in (12) is \(K_{G,ij}\).  Entrywise binomial expansion proves the exact identity
\[
Q_G=\sum_{r=1}^{k}\binom{k}{r}K_G^{\circ r}.
\tag{13}
\]
The matrix \(K_G\) is positive semidefinite because
\[
K_G=\frac1n(D_q^{-1}BP)(D_q^{-1}BP)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
To verify positivity after entrywise powers without importing an assumption, observe that if \(H_{ij}=\langle h_i,h_j\rangle\) and \(L_{ij}=\langle \ell_i,\ell_j\rangle\), then
\[
(H\circ L)_{ij}=\langle h_i\otimes\ell_i,h_j\otimes\ell_j\rangle,
\]
so \(H\circ L\) is positive semidefinite.  Iteration shows \(K_G^{\circ r}\succeq0\), and (13) gives \(Q_G\succeq0\).

We next bound its operator norm.  If \(K\succeq0\), \(a\ge\max_iK_{ii}>0\), and \(X\) is symmetric, then
\[
-\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}I\preceq X\preceq\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}I.
\]
The preceding tensor-Gram calculation shows that entrywise multiplication by \(K\) preserves both inequalities.  Since \(K\circ I=\operatorname{diag}(K_{ii})\preceq aI\),
\[
\|K\circ X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le a\|X\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Taking \(X=K^{\circ(r-1)}\) inductively and using (13) yields
\[
\|Q_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\|K_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\frac{(1+a)^k-1}{a}.
\tag{14}
\]
Here
\[
K_{G,ii}=\frac{m_i-m_i^2/n}{nq_i^2}=\frac{m_i}{n-m_i}
\le a_0:=\frac{M_n}{n-M_n},
\tag{15}
\]
and
\[
\|K_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\frac{\|BP\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}{n(1-M_n/n)^2},
\qquad
\frac{\|K_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{a_0}
\le\frac{\|BP\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2}{M_n(1-M_n/n)}.
\tag{16}
\]
The covariance definition of \(Q_G\) and the control endpoint bound give
\[
\operatorname{Var}(U_0\mid G)=\frac1{n^2}b^{\mathsf T}Q_Gb
\le\frac{\|Q_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n^2}\|b\|_2^2
\le\frac{\|Q_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}.
\tag{17}
\]
Since \(U_1-U_0\) is unbiased for \(\tau_n\), (11), (14)--(17), \((1+a_0)^k=(1-M_n/n)^{-k}\), and \((x-y)^2\le2x^2+2y^2\) imply
\[
\mathbb E[(U_1-U_0-\tau_n)^2\mid G]
\le\frac2k+
\frac{2\|B_2(G)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\{(1-M_n/n)^{-k}-1\}}
{nM_n(1-M_n/n)}
=U(G,k_n).
\tag{18}
\]

It remains to respect the prescribed observed-data sigma-field.  Let \(\mathcal F=\sigma(G,Z^{\mathrm{seed}},Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Potential outcomes are fixed, so conditioning additionally on \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}\) does not alter the conditional seed law given \(G,Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\).  Whenever \(J_\ell=i\), unit \(i\) is fully treated and \(y_i(Z^{\mathrm{seed}})=a_i\).  The control term is already \(\mathcal F\)-measurable.  Hence Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}rb\mbox{-}estimator}\) gives exactly
\[
\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}=\mathbb E[U_1-U_0\mid\mathcal F].
\]
The tower property proves unbiasedness, and conditional Jensen applied to \(U_1-U_0-\tau_n\) shows that the MSE of \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\) is no larger than (18).  Finally, \(B,m_i,h_{ij},q_i,\pi_i,K_G,Q_G\) are finite matrix or rational operations on \(G\), and each \(w_i(z;G)\) is obtained by finite summation over the seed tuples that induce \(z\).  This proves every assertion.
